featured_reviews.name: Deeva Ajmera
featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s my first ever time pinning down something as a review, and i am more than happy doing so. My cat Cece is nothing less than a soul mate to me, I breathe because she breathes. I’ve had relentlessly bad and suspicious experiences at big pet hospitals, clinics etc- who only focus on charging more than its worth, don’t really care about prompt diagnosis or correct advice, it’s all commercialisation. My gut couldn’t trust any one in past 2 years.

With God’s grace, I somehow came across Dr. Nitin’s Myraplus clinic recently and after reading the reviews, I couldn’t wait to meet him for Cece. She is currently going through some health related issues, and i’ve never been put at ease before like how Dr. Nitin has put me at ease. He is kind, calm, carefully and accurately explains everything which always puts me at ease. I tend to get extremely paranoid even when there’s slightest inconvenience to Cece, I cry until there’s no end;  but Dr. Nitin’s helpful vibe, confidence, behaviour, knowledge and genuineness gives me much relief - knowing that he is giving correct treatment to my baby Cece. He actually also focuses on administering minimal load of antibiotics which is great in a long run.

He is not money minded unlike other vets (which always made me worry about my baby’s health) ; rather he genuinely cares for and wants to help all kinds of animals (which are our lifelines)!

No unnecessary stress of consistent blood works for no reason, Myraplus has quite reasonable with their test prices too yet, on a side note. My baby Cece is currently been treated under Dr.Nitin’s care and till now I trust him a 100% with my gut for my baby :)
I believe y’ll should hit him up whenever in need :)

featured_reviews.name: Fatma Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve been taking my cat to Dr. Nitin for the past one and a half years, and I can genuinely say he’s the best veterinarian we’ve ever had. My cat has been through some serious health issues, and he has saved her from illnesses that could have taken her life.

Before finding him, I visited many vets, but no one ever treated my cat—or even me—the way he does. He’s patient, gentle, and truly cares about animals. He explains everything clearly, never rushes, and always gives the right treatment at the right time.

I trust him completely with my cat’s health. If anyone is looking for a vet who treats your pet like family, Dr. Nitin is the one. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Vishva Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
We trusted this clinic with our 2-year-old cat during the most critical time of his life, and today we are left with heartbreak, trauma, and serious doubts about the care he received.

Our cat was already battling pleural effusion/FIP-related illness, but after the second drainage procedure done at this clinic, his condition worsened dramatically. Unlike the first drainage done elsewhere after which he breathed better and stabilized this time he developed pneumothorax and his breathing never improved afterward.

We were never properly prepared for how unstable his condition had become post-procedure. We also specifically informed the staff that our cat became extremely frightened and aggressive when touched without us present, and requested that he not be unnecessarily handled while we briefly stepped out. Despite that, he was taken out and handled. When we returned, we were met with his lifeless body.

Maybe no one can say with certainty what would have changed the outcome. But as pet parents who watched the drastic difference between the first and second procedures, we cannot ignore the feeling that mistakes, inadequate handling, or complications during treatment may have contributed to his final deterioration.

Losing a pet is devastating enough. Being left with unanswered questions and guilt afterward makes it even harder.

I hope this clinic learns to communicate more transparently, handle critical patients more carefully, and show greater sensitivity toward animals who are already terrified and struggling to survive.

featured_reviews.name: sms sweta
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a pet parent, I’m sure many of you will understand the kind of fear and helplessness we feel when something isn’t right with our baby. I went through exactly that when my 14-year-old feline, Goldie, was diagnosed with a serious tumour on her left paw. Those days were filled with worry, questions, and uncertainty.

All we knew was that we needed the right oncologist — someone we could trust completely. That’s when we found the incredible team at Superpets, and from that very first visit, everything began to feel a little lighter.

From explaining the diagnosis and possible causes, to guiding us through every test, every step was handled with so much patience, clarity, and compassion. What truly stood out was how reassuring the entire team was — always available to answer questions, clear doubts, and take that extra effort to make both us and Goldie feel comfortable.

The journey — from diagnosis, to surgery, to post-operative care and stitch removal — was smoother than we could have ever hoped for. Every decision they made felt right, thoughtful, and in Goldie’s best interest.

A special note of gratitude to Dr. Pratyush, Dr. Vasudha, and Dr. Gauri — you are truly angels in disguise. The care, dedication, and gentleness with which you handled Goldie means the world to us. It’s not just medical expertise, but your genuine love for animals that makes all the difference.

I must admit, I was initially skeptical about traveling all the way from the suburbs to Bandra for treatment — but today, I can say with complete conviction that every visit, every effort, was absolutely worth it.

What touched me deeply was that even after a month, Dr. Pratyush personally followed up to check on Goldie’s health. That level of care is rare and speaks volumes about the kind of people they are — not just doctors, but true lifesavers.

This entire experience has been a journey of gratitude. People like them are not just treating animals — they are healing families.

Thank you, Superpets team, from the bottom of my heart, for taking such beautiful care of our baby.

Forever grateful. 🙏🏻

featured_reviews.name: Smitaa Nair
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is a blessing. My German shepherd champ was taken to super pets in an emergency situation. He had developed something called GDV. I was unaware if this situation being a pet parent since more than 17 years now (I have had pets since several years) After taking him to vetic hospital for emergency (which was extremely careless and didn’t even treat it like emergency) post his X-ray on recommendation from some friends I rushed him to super pets. They immediately took charge of the situation. He underwent operation and was discharged in 5 days. We had to take him for regular follow ups and on a follow up in a weeks time, doctors suspected something wrong and again on further tests discovered that his spleen had got affected and damaged along with few further conditions that had developed. He underwent second surgery. He battled for his life for a month in this hospital. He was hospitalised. The care, affection and love he recieved along with the proper medical care is nothing less than a gift for parents seeing their child fight for life and death each day. Inspite of he being aggressive he was pampered and taken care of as if he belongs to them. His entire body had collapsed and post 1 month he finally got discharged. He had lost his ability to walk post all this condition as his hip and spine had got affected. We continued Physio with them. It’s October today. My boy got discharged in June and we are in our way for our regular Physio all hail and hearty, not just walking but running and bullying my other 2 dogs :) No words can thank them enough. His recovery is nothing less than a miracle only because of timely care and attention given to him by the super vets at super pets.

featured_reviews.name: vikas nalawade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review about a stray cat named “Leopard” who eventually became our family member. Request you to please read it till end, as it may be helpful to any pet parent.
Leopard met with an accident and was missing for a week’s period. Later we found him & we noticed that he had a fracture at shoulder of right forelimb. Doctors told us that leg needs to be operated by inserting rod in his leg, so we got him operated by Dr. Sunetra. The surgery went well, but three days after surgery, Leopard's operated leg started swelling, we informed Dr. Sunetra but she told us it is the swelling due to surgery and it will subside downwards. But that swelling was due to infection and it lead to pus formation. Next day the swelling increased and in the evening pus started oozing out, seeing this we called up Dr. Sunetra & rushed to her with our Leopard. Dr. told us to keep flushing the wound twice a day with betadine. After 2-3 days of this treatment, the skin around the infected area went dead and we had a clear sight of his wound with operated area, where we could see his bone from two points because healing was not completed & the stitches were opened. We even asked Dr. Sunetra the doubt in our mind that this infection will not spread in his operated leg & internal body, to which she responded, it would not.
Eventually his external pain reduced but he had internal pain, which we failed to understand. He could not tolerate the pain and stopped eating and got fever exactly on 8th day from operation. We informed this situation of Leopard at every visit to Dr. Sunetra, but she recommended to force feed our Leopard. Later on our Leopard left with no energy to walk on his own and lift his neck, he even started heavy breathing. After informing this situation to Dr. Sunetra, she then advised us to put saline for his recovery but nowhere had she conveyed that Leopard’s health is deteriorating & he needs hospitalization. At this time, she was going out of town & was not available for 4-5 days.
Since, Dr. Sunetra was not available, we went to other Vet doctor who knew Leopard's medical history. This doctor told us to continue saline treatment twice a day for at least 4-5 days. Here the blood test was also done to examine the condition of our Leopard, where the report came with alarming & critical output depicting WBC increased & Platelets dropped to severe condition. Even this doctor also not recommended that our Leopard require hospitalization. This was the 11th day after operation.
The 12th day story (i.e. 1st July 23) of our Leopard was worst. The morning session of his saline was completed & even this second doctor went out of town for 3-4 days without recommending hospitalization. By evening, somewhere from 4:30pm, the heavy breathing became worse & we could not see his pain. We started calling Dr. Sunetra, but her phone was not reachable, so we text her on WhatsApp along with Leopard’s blood report. Since no response from doctor, with Leopard, we rushed to a Vet hospital, where he was admitted with a note by the doctors, like heavy breathing & drop in body temperature, which was very critical condition. He was kept in ICU incubator with oxygen supply to ease his breathe & improve his body temperature. The hospital doctors even told us that there are chances that the infection might have spread into blood. Unfortunately battling with pain & breathing problem our Leopard passed away on the same day around 11 pm.
There are certain questions for Dr. Sunetra;
# Why you haven't included any medicine for infection post-surgery?
# Why you did not advised us prior to start saline, when we informed you that Leopard lost his appetite?
# Why you did not look closely if the infection was spreading in the body? If you think it wasn't then why did he lost his appetite, had weakness, got fever, started heavy breathing?
# Why you took everything so lightly and casually in his case? Was it because it was a stray cat?

The doctor’s entire focus was on the operated area and the wound & the rest health parameters were ignored completely.

featured_reviews.review_text:
"PLEASE READ BEFORE ENTRUSTING YOUR PET HERE"

I am sharing my experience so that other pet parents can make informed decisions and hopefully avoid the pain and trauma I have gone through.

My dog, Lambhorgini, was admitted to this veterinary hospital on 17 December 2025 at approximately 11:00 PM. The veterinarian on duty insisted that he be admitted for “better treatment” and informed us that pet parents were not allowed to stay back in the hospital. Trusting the professional advice given, we agreed to the admission.

At the time of admission, he was placed on oxygen and, while I was present, appeared to be stabilizing and recovering. At no point was I informed that his condition was critical or that his life was at immediate risk.

The following morning, I was informed that he had passed away at an estimated time of 8:30 AM.

What has been most distressing is not only the sudden loss of my deeply loved pet, but the lack of communication, transparency, and responsibility throughout the process. Even post-event, no clear explanation or accountability was provided by the designated veterinarian on duty at the time.

As a pet parent from Singapore, I am extremely disappointed by the quality, efficiency, and professionalism experienced at this facility. Entrusting a beloved companion to a hospital should come with honest updates, proper communication, and accountability — all of which were lacking in this experience.

Based on what I went through, I would strongly advise other pet parents not to entrust their pets to this facility at any given time. Pets deserve competent care and responsible medical oversight, especially during critical situations.

I am sharing this review solely so that other pet parents can make an informed choice and do not experience the same heartbreak.

Sakeena Thakker , pet parent of Lambhorgini

featured_reviews.name: Ivana Dutta
featured_reviews.review_text:
I brought my cat to Andheri Vetic clinic at 4AM from Thane due to sudden breathing problems. The X-ray showed fluid in his lungs, which required urgent intervention.

During the treatment, my cat was placed on oxygen support, but the equipment used was a makeshift paper cup with a pipe, which I had to hold myself to keep it on his face. When the clinic staff attempted to proceed with a procedure, the oxygen delivery was not maintained properly. My cat panicked, and due to insufficient oxygen support during handling, he unfortunately passed away.

I observed that the staff handling my cat seemed inexperienced and did not follow standard emergency protocols for a cat in respiratory distress, such as using a proper oxygen mask or securing him safely before attempting a procedure.

I am sharing this experience so that other pet owners can be aware and so the clinic can review their emergency procedures and staff training. Proper equipment, calm handling, and continuous oxygen are essential in critical cases like this.

featured_reviews.name: Mrunmayi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Zero stars for this hospital. I admitted my 25-30 days-old kitten for a viral infection, and he was already in a critical condition. However, the doctors here did not put much effort into saving him. Both the senior and junior doctors kept saying that he had a viral infection and that his chances of survival were very low.
I also observed that all the senior doctors were always in the OPD section, while only junior doctors were present in the IPD section. These junior doctors did not seem to know what treatment had been given to my pet by the previous doctors before their shift.
When I went to see my pet in the evening, his condition had worsened significantly. The doctor on duty said they were trying to draw his blood for a CBC test, but no proper treatment had been provided to him at that time. When I insisted that secondary treatment be started, they finally gave him antibiotics.
At my previous veterinary clinic, I was advised to give oral feeding to my kitten every two hours. However, when I informed the staff here, they simply acknowledged it but did not feed him. Instead, they said they were waiting for him to stabilize before giving oral feed, otherwise he might collapse.
They also overcharged me for everything. Even very small doses of medicine cost ₹800. When I asked the receptionist about this, she was rude and disrespectful. She said they were charging only for the doses given, even though my kitten required only a 0.5 ml dose, and that the rest of the medicine is used for multiple patients, not just my kitten.
I am attaching the invoice for reference, as well as the bill from my previous hospital, so the difference can be clearly seen.
If you truly want to save your pet, do not bring them here. They seem more focused on making money from sick animals. The doctors also indirectly suggest that your pet is not going to survive.
My experience with this hospital was extremely bad.
If you want, I can also create a more powerful, formal Google review version that gets maximum attention and response from management.
